item.title: [Episode 27] Tokyo's Skyline ([27화] 도쿄의 스카이라인)
item.description:
[Episode 27] Tokyo's Skyline ([27화] 도쿄의 스카이라인)

☞ View from Episode 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introduction (☞ 등장인물 소개)

Three months after Sariel’s successful debut, Evan transferred from the Korean branch to the Japanese branch. (사리엘의 성공적인 데뷔 3개월 후, 에반은 한국 지사에서 일본 지사로 자리를 옮겼다.)

Evan began his new journey in a 33-story mansion in Tokyo's Minato-ku, designated by the company. While scrolling on his smartphone in the living room, he looked up to see the Tokyo cityscape spread out beyond the mansion's signature floor-to-ceiling windows. The orderly roads and the forest of silver buildings seemed to hold everything in its place. (에반은 회사가 지정한 도쿄 미나토구 33층 맨션에서 새 여정을 시작했다. 거실에서 스마트폰을 스크롤링하다 고개를 들자 맨션 특유의 통유리창 너머로 도쿄 시내가 펼쳐졌다. 질서 정연하게 뻗은 도로와 은색 빌딩 숲이 모든 것을 제자리에 가둬놓은 듯했다.)

Gazing out the window, leaving the bitter taste of espresso on his tongue, Evan scrolled down his email window. (에반은 창밖을 바라보다 에스프레소의 쓴맛을 혀끝에 남긴 채, 이메일 창을 하단으로 내렸다.)

Subject: Transfer Confirmation — APAC Strategy Director, Tokyo (Subject: Transfer Confirmation — APAC Strategy Director, Tokyo)

It was the confirmation email for his promotion and transfer that HR had sent two weeks ago. (2주 전, HR이 보내준 승진 인사 확정 메일이었다.)

It wasn't that he had been chasing success over the past decade since his discharge from Iraq. The driving force behind Evan rolling on the floor of the DMZ and burning the midnight oil writing proposals in a tiny room in Pyeongtaek was his mindset to overcome the "Three-Second Ghost" through his creation, Sariel. (이라크 제대 후 지난 십여 년간 출세를 좇은 것은 아니었다. 에반이 휴전선 바닥을 뒹굴고, 평택 골방에서 밤새워 제안서를 썼던 원동력은, 사리엘이라는 작품으로 ‘3초의 망령’을 극복하려는 마음가짐이었다.)

Nevertheless, the event of a promotion was clearly a significant milestone in his life, allowing him to feel a sense of accomplishment from his work for the first time in a long while. (그럼에도 승진이라는 이벤트는 분명, 꽤 오랜만에 자신이 해온 일에 보람을 느낄 수 있는 인생의 마일스톤이었다.)

Just a few months ago, he had only been staring at the concrete walls of Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek, but now Tokyo's entire skyline was framed within his window. (몇 달 전까지 평택 기지의 콘크리트 벽만 보고 있었는데, 이젠 도쿄의 스카이라인이 통째로 창 안에 들어왔다.)

"Evan, look over there. You can really see Mount Fuji." (“에반, 저기 좀 봐. 후지산이 진짜 보여.”)

Irina came into the living room with a still-sleepy voice. When Evan said he had to go to Tokyo, she didn't hesitate to board the plane with him. (이리나가 잠이 덜 깬 목소리로 거실에 나왔다. 그녀는 에반이 도쿄로 가야 한다고 하자, 주저 없이 도쿄행 비행기에 같이 몸을 실었다.)

"I'm making enough money. Just come with me." (“돈은 충분히 벌고 있어. 몸만 따라와 줘.”)

That was Evan's offer, and for Irina, that one sentence was enough. (그것이 에반의 제의였고, 이리나에게는 그 말 한마디면 충분했다.)

Being an experienced bodyguard, she could find part-time work in any city, so Irina adapted quickly in Tokyo. The symbiotic relationship they had built up through London, Poland, and Pyeongtaek continued naturally into Tokyo. (숙련된 경호원은 어느 도시에서든 파트타임 일자리를 구할 수 있었기에, 이리나는 도쿄에서도 금세 적응했다. 런던과 폴란드, 평택을 거치며 쌓인 둘의 공생 관계는 도쿄까지도 자연스레 이어졌다.)

"See, I told you. I said you'd have great career success this year. Getting promoted and even coming to Japan. My app was spot on." (“거봐, 내가 뭐랬어. 올해 당신이 커리어적으로 크게 성공한다고 했잖아. 승진해서 일본으로까지 오게 되고. 내 앱이 정확했다니까.”)

Standing by the marble table with a piece of toast in her mouth, Irina began scrolling through her astrology app. With a slight smile lingering in her eyes, she swiped her thumb frantically before turning the screen towards Evan. (이리나는 대리석 식탁에 서서 토스트를 입에 문 채 점성술 앱을 훑기 시작했다. 잔웃음이 남은 눈으로 정신없이 엄지를 쓸어내리던 그녀가, 화면을 에반 쪽으로 돌렸다.)

[Today's Transit][Venus is passing through your partner's 7th House. This is the section where the orbits of the two of you come closest. Luck in love is on the rise, and your mutual dependence becomes a structure, not a weakness.][MN1] ([오늘의 트랜짓][금성이 파트너의 7하우스를 통과하고 있습니다. 두 사람의 궤도가 가장 가까워지는 구간입니다. 애정운은 상승 기류를 타고, 서로에 대한 의존은 약점이 아니라 구조가 됩니다.][MN1] )

"Did you hear that? Dependence is a structure, not a weakness. The app knows us better than we know ourselves." (“들었지? 의존은 약점이 아니라 구조래. 앱이 우리보다 우리를 잘 알아.”)

As Irina read aloud with delight, her expression froze at the next card. (기분 좋은 듯 소리 내어 읽던 이리나의 표정이 다음 카드에서 굳었다.)

[Caution: Mars enters Capricorn][The planet of action, Mars, stands cold and still at the peak of your partner's 10th House, the pinnacle of career. Shadows are cast alongside the place of achievement. Accidents occur on familiar paths, from unexpected angles.][MN2] ([주의: 화성, 염소자리 진입][행동의 행성 화성이 파트너의 10하우스, 커리어의 정점 위에서 차갑게 멈춥니다. 성취의 자리에는 그림자가 함께 배치됩니다. 사고는 익숙한 동선에서, 예상하지 못한 각도로 찾아옵니다.][MN2] )

"Evan... it says there could be an unexpected accident?" (“에반… 예상치 못한 사고가 날 수 있다는데?”)

Evan unconsciously rubbed his left fingertips. (에반은 무의식적으로 왼손 손가락 끝을 만지작거렸다.)

"My life is decided by algorithms. Not by the positions of stars." (“내 인생은 알고리즘이 결정해. 별자리 위치가 아니라.”)

"There are things algorithms can't catch," Irina's voice lost its playfulness. "Unexpected accidents can happen anytime, not just from fortune telling. What's scarier than that is you freezing up again at that critical moment when I'm not there." (“알고리즘이 못 잡는 것도 있어.” 이리나의 목소리에서 장난기가 빠졌다. “예상치 못한 사고는 점괘가 아니어도 언제든 일어나. 그것보다 무서운 건, 내가 없을 때 당신이 그 찰나에 또 멈춰버리는 거야.”)

Evan adjusted his tie and answered nonchalantly, but Irina's intuition picked up on a strange chill. She added with a pout. (에반은 넥타이를 매만지며 심드렁하게 대답했지만, 이리나의 직관은 묘한 한기를 잡아냈다. 그녀가 뾰루퉁한 표정으로 덧붙였다.)

"Evan, there's no harm in being careful." (“에반, 조심해서 나쁠 건 없잖아.”)

"Got it. I'll be careful." (“알겠어. 조심할게.”)

"I'm recording that." (“그 말 녹음해둔다.”)

Leaving Irina's sharp-tongued joke behind, Evan headed out for his first day of work. (이리나의 뼈 있는 농담을 뒤로하고 에반은 첫 출근길에 올랐다.)

His destination was Toranomon, not far from the mansion. An area dense with Tokyo's wealthy, large law firms, and global corporations. Dudal Japan occupied an entire floor of the tallest building there. The atmosphere was completely different from the fortress-like office in Pyeongtaek. (목적지는 맨션에서 멀지 않은 토라노몬이었다. 도쿄의 부유층과 대형 로펌, 글로벌 기업들이 밀집한 구역. 듀다엘 재팬은 그곳에서도 가장 높은 빌딩 한 층을 통째로 사용했다. 평택의 군사 요새 같은 사무실과는 공기부터 달랐다.)

"Evan Yoon? So you're the famous APAC strategy lead!" (“에반 윤? 당신이 그 유명한 APAC 전략 담당자!”)

Mark, the American Vice President of the Japan branch, lightly tapped Evan's shoulder as he guided him around the office. There was a characteristic, manufactured, energetic vibe in his gestures. (일본 지사의 미국인 부지사장 마크가 에반의 어깨를 가볍게 치며 사무실을 안내했다. 미국인 특유의 가공된 활기찬 기운이 몸짓에서 느껴졌다.)

"This is the break room, over there is the analysis team. Let me know if you have any questions." (“여기는 휴게실, 저쪽은 분석팀. 궁금한 거 있으면 언제든 말해.”)

As Evan passed by, the Japanese employees didn't take their eyes off their monitors. Mark didn't seem to notice. Only the sound of keyboards filled the tense silence. Mark was someone who had long given up on reading the room. (에반이 지나가는 동안 일본인 직원들은 모니터에서 눈을 떼지 않았다. 마크는 눈치채지 못하는 것 같았다. 키보드 소리만이 팽팽한 정적을 메웠다. 마크는 오래전에 분위기 파악을 포기한 사람이었다.)

Evan felt it as a wall. (에반은 그것을 벽으로 느꼈다.)

Instead of Sariel's blue interface, the local employees' monitors were full of Excel sheets and mechanical drawings reviewing compatibility with local Japanese vendors. Though the matrix organization structure mixed employees of various nationalities, the Japanese staff stayed strictly within their inner circle. They seemed to view Evan not as a technical expert, but as a monitor sent from headquarters. (현지 직원들의 모니터에는 사리엘의 파란색 인터페이스 대신, 일본 로컬 업체들과의 호환성을 검토하는 엑셀 시트와 기계 도면이 가득했다. 매트릭스 조직이라는 이름 아래 여러 국적의 직원을 섞어 놓았지만, 일본 직원들은 철저하게 자신들의 이너 서클 안에 머물렀다. 에반을 기술 전문가가 아니라 본사에서 보낸 감시자로 여기는 듯했다.)

"Alright, that's the end of the office tour. The Branch Manager wants to see you, so head over there." (“자 그럼 사무실 소개는 이걸로 끝났고, 지사장님이 보자니까 저기로 가면 돼.”)

Evan headed to the office of Kenji Tanaka, the Branch Manager of Dudal Japan. It was an executive office with a panoramic view of Tokyo Tower. Tanaka gestured towards the reception sofa. (에반은 듀다엘 일본 지사장 다나카 켄지의 방으로 향했다. 도쿄타워가 한눈에 보이는 임원실이었다. 다나카가 응접 소파를 손바닥으로 가리켰다.)

"Team Lead Evan, I'll be honest with you. The Japanese government is not happy." (“에반 팀장, 솔직히 말할게요. 일본 정부는 곤란해하고 있어요.”)

Tanaka started talking business without any preamble. Speaking in fluent English, he didn't seem like the typical Japanese boss. (다나카는 다짜고짜 일 얘기부터 시작했다. 유창한 영어로 말하는 것이 전형적인 일본인 상사는 아닌 것 같았다.)

"The problem is that while they inwardly acknowledge Sariel's performance, their pride is hurt. There's significant resistance to belatedly adopting a system that Korea introduced first." (“사리엘의 성능은 내심 인정하면서도 자존심에 상처를 입은 게 문제예요. 한국이 먼저 도입한 시스템을 뒤늦게 따라가는 데 대한 거부감이 상당하다는 말이에요.”)

"After Sariel's first public demonstration last time?" (“지난번 사리엘 첫 공개 이후요?”)

"The Japanese media went crazy back then. While the Chief Cabinet Secretary just kept repeating 'under review,' Korea had already disclosed the coordinates. The government lost face internally." (“그때 일본 언론이 뒤집어졌으니까. 관방장관이 ‘분석 중’만 반복하는 사이 한국은 좌표까지 공개했잖아. 정부 내부에서 체면이 구겨진 거죠.”)

Tanaka took a gulp of the Pepsi sitting on his desk. (다나카가 탁상에 놓인 펩시를 한 모금 들이켰다.)

"Internally, they're using doubts about whether 'Korean-style optimization' fits the Japanese archipelago as a shield. Questioning whether an algorithm tuned for mountainous terrain can handle the noise generated by the Pacific's complex coastline and tens of thousands of islands." (“내부적으로는 ‘한국형 최적화’가 일본 열도에도 맞느냐는 의구심을 방패로 쓰고 있어요. 산악 지형에 맞춰진 알고리즘이 태평양의 복잡한 해안선과 수만 개의 섬에서 발생할 노이즈를 감당할 수 있겠느냐는 거죠.”)

"That's technically manageable. Past marine environment simulations have already..." (“그건 기술적으로 대응 가능합니다. 과거 해양 환경 시뮬레이션을 이미…")

"Mm... technically, that's not the issue," Tanaka cut Evan off. "Ultimately, it's a domestic political problem." (“음… 정확히는 기술 문제가 아니에요.” 다나카가 에반의 말을 잘랐다. “결국 국내 정치 문제인 거죠.”)

Tanaka gave a wry smile. (다나카가 쓴웃음을 지었다.)

"They want Sariel to become Japan's digital lighthouse in Yonaguni and Okinawa, but they fear Chinese retaliation. They've seen what happened to Korea. So, they've presented us with an offset trade bill." (“사리엘이 요나구니와 오키나와에서 일본의 디지털 등대가 되어주길 바라면서도, 중국의 보복은 두려워해요. 한국이 당한 꼴을 봤으니까. 그러면서 우리에겐 절충 교역이라는 청구서를 내밀었어요.”)

Offset trade. A transaction method where the buyer requires the seller to make reciprocal purchases or local investments equivalent to the contract value. (절충 교역. 무기를 사주는 대가로 비슷한 금액의 무기를 되사거나 현지 투자를 요구하는 거래 방식이다.)

But Japan's situation was a bit more complicated. (하지만 일본은 사정이 조금 더 복잡했다.)

"The Japanese government is apparently demanding Shirakawa Heavy Industries as a partner." (“일본 정부는 파트너로 시라카와 중공업을 요구하고 있다고 하네요.”)

Tanaka's voice dropped. (다나카의 목소리가 낮아졌다.)

"Shirakawa isn't just a company. It's the final stop for retired Ministry of Defense officials parachuting into new jobs—what they call 'amakudari.' They were a giant that sustained the empire's pride during WWII, building battleships and fighter planes, but were effectively shrunk into a local company by Article 9 of the Peace Constitution. They dream of a global resurgence through deregulation, but internal corruption and inefficiency make them both impossible to discard and difficult to keep for the Japanese government—a real white elephant." (“시라카와는 단순한 기업이 아니에요. 방위성 퇴직 관료들이 재취업하는 낙하산의 종착역, 흔히들 아마쿠다리라고 부르죠. 2차 대전 당시 전함과 전투기를 만들며 제국의 자존심을 지탱했던 거인인데, 평화헌법 9조에 묶여 로컬 기업으로 쪼그라들었다고 봐야죠. 규제 완화로 글로벌 시장 재도약을 꿈꾸고 있지만, 내부 부패와 비효율로 일본 정부에는 버릴 수도 안고 갈 수도 없는 계륵이라고나 할까요.”)

"Similar to Korea's Taesan Defense, yet different." (“한국의 태산디펜스와 비슷하면서도 다르군요.”)

Tanaka nodded. (다나카가 고개를 끄덕였다.)

"Shirakawa's technological level is still higher, but they lost their drive and will for expansion at some point. Only the political connections survived. The Japanese government's plan might be to use Sariel as an oxygen tank for Shirakawa." (“시라카와 쪽이 아직 기술력 수준은 더 높지만, 어느 시점에서 확장의 동력과 의지를 잃었어요. 정치적 연줄만 살아남은 거죠. 일본 정부는 사리엘을 시라카와의 산소 호흡기로 쓰겠다는 복안이 아닐까요.”)

"For now, I'll review the situation." (“일단, 상황을 검토해 보겠습니다.”)

Evan returned to his desk. A package from West Coast Labs had been delivered to one side of his desk. A note attached said it was a Sariel-compatible smartglass prototype for field testing. (에반은 자리로 돌아왔다. 책상 한쪽에 웨스트코스트랩에서 보낸 소포가 배달됐다. 사리엘 연동형 스마트글라스 시제품, 필드 테스트용이라는 메모가 붙어 있었다.)

Just as he was about to open the package, his iPhone vibrated. It was a video meeting request from Jeff. Jeff had also just been promoted, based on the Sariel Korea deployment success, to Managing Director of the Global Strategy Team at the Virginia headquarters. (소포를 뜯으려던 순간, 아이폰이 진동했다. 제프의 화상 미팅 요청이었다. 사리엘 한국 도입을 성과로 인정받아 버지니아 본사의 글로벌 전략팀 매니징 디렉터로 같이 막 승진했던 터였다.)

"Evan, long time no see. Like the Tokyo scenery?" (“에반, 오랜만이야. 도쿄 풍경이 좋나?”)

"Yes. What's the matter?" (“예, 용건은 무엇인지요.”)

"You're going to be incredibly busy from now on." (“앞으로 엄청 바빠질 거야.”)

Jeff's voice on the screen was a pitch higher than during his time in Korea. It felt like a degree of arrogance had risen along with the promotion. (화면 속 제프의 목소리는 한국 시절보다 무언가 한 톤 더 올라갔다. 직급이 올라간 만큼 거드름도 한층 더 올라간 느낌이었다.)

"The company didn't send you to Tokyo to enjoy sushi. The will of HQ is to enmesh all of Asia in Sariel's network." (“회사가 당신을 도쿄로 보낸 건, 거기서 스시나 즐기라는 뜻이 아니야. 아시아 전체를 사리엘의 그물망에 넣으라는 게 본사의 의지야.”)

"The complicated situation with the Japanese government needs to be sorted out first..." (“일본 정부 쪽 복잡한 상황을 먼저 정리해야…”)

"Japan can't avoid buying it anyway. Don't sweat it too much," Jeff cut in. "A defense expo is coming up soon in Manila. I need you to manage our booth there." (“일본은 어차피 안 사고는 못 배겨. 너무 힘 빼지 마.” 제프가 잘랐다. “조만간 마닐라에서 방산 전시회가 열리는데, 거기서 부스 운영 맡아줘.”)

"Manila?" (“마닐라요?”)

"What, don't like business trips to 'developing countries'?" (“왜, 후진국 출장은 싫어?”)

"No, sir. I'll prepare." (“아뇨. 준비하겠습니다.”)

"The core of this trip isn't just Japan, it's a sales strategy targeting even the Philippine military. A big picture tying together the entire Asia-Pacific region. Directives from top management." (“이번 출장의 핵심은 일본이 아니라 필리핀 군까지 염두에 둔 세일즈 전략이야. 아시아-태평양 전체를 묶는 큰 그림. 경영진의 지시야.”)

Jeff lifted the rim of his glasses perched on his nose as he uttered the phrase 'directives from top management.' (제프는 경영진의 지시라는 단어를 내뱉으면서 코 끝에 얹힌 안경테를 치켜세웠다.)

Various discussions followed, and the video conference ended after an hour. Evan closed his laptop and left the office. (이런저런 얘기가 이어지며 화상 회의는 1시간 만에 끝났다. 에반은 노트북을 덮고 사무실을 나섰다.)

Beyond the clear Tokyo sky, a tropical depression began to move northward from the south. (도쿄의 맑은 하늘 너머, 남쪽에서 열대 저기압이 북상하기 시작했다.)

item.title: Former Navy Secretary: "Pursued Another US Shipyard Project with Hanwha During Tenure, Beyond Philadelphia" (前해군장관 “재임 중 한화와 필리 外 또 다른 美조선소 사업 추진”)
item.description:
Former Navy Secretary: "Pursued Another US Shipyard Project with Hanwha During Tenure, Beyond Philadelphia" (前해군장관 “재임 중 한화와 필리 外 또 다른 美조선소 사업 추진”)

Former U.S. Navy Secretary John Phelan stated on the 15th, "The United States needs new shipyards and trained personnel," adding, "We sought to pursue another shipyard project in cooperation with Hanwha, which has achieved excellent results by acquiring the Philadelphia shipyard. While I cannot disclose the name, the goal was to have Hanwha expand its operations in the U.S. and play a greater role in transferring its technology and expertise to America." Phelan, a billionaire businessman and close associate of President Donald Trump, served as Navy Secretary from March 2025 to April this year, leading efforts to revive the U.S. shipbuilding industry and engaging in U.S.-Korea shipbuilding cooperation. <<> Speaking at the Aspen Security Forum (ASF) held in Aspen, Colorado, on the same day, Phelan responded to a question about why countries like South Korea can build more ships than the U.S., saying, "South Korea has adopted more modern technologies, such as robotics." Phelan visited South Korea last April and toured HD Hyundai Heavy Industries' Ulsan shipyard. He noted, "When a welder presses a button, someone brings components, so they can just keep welding, whereas the U.S. lacks such a system," and "Even in the nuclear submarine construction site in Connecticut, digital twin technology was not applied to the design, so we had to introduce it." He also remarked on the shipbuilding industry, saying, "There's a characteristic that the more ships you build, the faster the work becomes," and "The fact that people in a village have been working for five generations is something to learn from South Korea and Japan." <<> Phelan said, "China is currently building over 1,700 ships annually, while the U.S. builds only five. The gap is widening. China has a shipyard large enough to fit all of America's shipyards, which is absurd." During his tenure, he actively pursued U.S.-Korea shipbuilding cooperation and indicated that he explored Hanwha's acquisition of additional shipyards in the U.S. Michael Coulter, CEO of Hanwha Defense USA, had stated in January this year that the Philadelphia shipyard, with only two docks, could not meet manufacturing demand, saying, "We are reviewing options to expand production capacity and storage space." Phelan also shared, "There were areas where we were somewhat lacking, so we also considered building parts of the hull in other countries or regions." <<> Trump is known to have encouraged Phelan to revive the shipbuilding industry, even showing him pictures of ships in the early morning. Phelan noted, "Professional personnel like welders and electricians are things that artificial intelligence (AI) cannot solve or replace," and argued for fairer wages to attract such workers. He also said, "The Navy fails to leverage any purchasing scale advantages in contract work, lacking business common sense, so there were really many things that needed improvement." Stepping down abruptly in April this year, he remarked, "Entering an organization like the Pentagon, which is extremely risk-averse, and insisting on taking risks inevitably ruffles a lot of people's feathers and makes them uneasy," but added, "I may have pushed too hard, but I have no regrets about what I did as Navy Secretary." <<> <<> ◇ ☞Aspen Institute <<> The Aspen Institute is a nonprofit organization founded in 1949 by American businessman Walter Paepcke in Aspen, Colorado. Originally from Chicago, Paepcke was inspired by Aspen's natural scenery and conceived the idea for world leaders to step away from their routines and engage in discussions. Its mission is "to solve the most important challenges facing the United States and the world through dialogue and leadership." It aims to be a bipartisan facilitator that steps back from political polarization to convene diverse participants for discussion. Over 30 programs operate independently in fields such as economics, education, and the environment. Since 2010, it has held the annual Aspen Security Forum, where global diplomacy and security experts discuss domestic and international issues. (존 펠런 전 미 해군 장관은 15일 “미국은 새로운 조선소와 훈련된 인력이 필요하다”며 “필라델피아 조선소를 인수해 훌륭한 성과를 내고 있는 한화와 협력해 또 다른 조선소 사업을 추진하려 했다. 이름은 밝힐 수 없으나 한화가 미국 내 사업을 확장하고, 그들이 가진 기술과 노하우를 미국으로 이전하는 데 더 많은 역할을 하도록 만들게 하는 것이었다”고 했다. 억만장자 사업가 출신이자 도널드 트럼프 대통령의 측근인 펠런은 2025년 3월부터 올해 4월까지 해군 장관을 지내며 미국의 조선업 부활을 주도하고 한미 조선 협력에도 관여해 온 인물이다.)

item.title: "Korea’s Uranium Enrichment, a Sensitive Issue… Must Proceed in an Orderly and Cautious Manner" (“한국의 우라늄 농축, 민감한 문제… 질서 있고 신중하게 진행해야“)
item.description:
"Korea’s Uranium Enrichment, a Sensitive Issue… Must Proceed in an Orderly and Cautious Manner" (“한국의 우라늄 농축, 민감한 문제… 질서 있고 신중하게 진행해야“)

As the U.S. government pushes to revitalize the nuclear industry in response to the surging electricity demand in the era of artificial intelligence (AI), former Deputy Secretary of Energy Daniel Poneman (70) said in an interview with this newspaper on the 14th, "I far prefer to see the U.S. and Korea cooperate very solidly and successfully sell nuclear reactors around the world, rather than letting Russia and China dominate the market." Poneman served as the Deputy Secretary of Energy, the second-highest position at the Department of Energy (DOE), from 2009 to 2014 during the Obama administration, and was CEO of Centrus Energy, a U.S. nuclear energy company, from 2015 to 2023. Regarding the fact sheet that specifies U.S. support for a process that would lead to civilian uranium enrichment and reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel, he called it a "sensitive issue" but added, "If we proceed in a thoughtful, orderly manner, I can envision a future where uranium enrichment takes place in Korea." (인공지능(AI) 시대 폭증하는 전력 수요를 맞아 미국 정부가 원자력 산업 부흥에 나선 가운데, 대니얼 폰먼(70) 전 에너지부 부장관은 14일 본지 인터뷰에서 “러시아와 중국이 시장 주도권을 잡는 것 보다는, 미국과 한국이 매우 탄탄하게 협력해 전 세계에 원자로를 성공적으로 판매하는 모습을 훨씬 더 선호한다”고 했다. 폰먼은 오바마 정부 때인 2009~2014년 에너지부(DOE) 2인자인 부장관을 지냈고, 2015~2023년 미국 내 원자력 기업인 센트러스 에너지 최고경영자(CEO)를 지냈다. ‘민간 우라늄 농축 및 사용후 핵연료 재처리로 귀결될 절차’에 대한 미국 측 지지를 명시한 팩트시트(Fact Sheet·공동 설명 자료)에 대해 “민감한 문제”라면서도 “신중하고 질서 있게(thoughtful, orderly manner) 진행한다면 한국에서 우라늄 농축이 이뤄지는 미래를 그려볼 수 있다고 생각한다”고 했다.)

Poneman, met at the Aspen Security Forum (ASF) opening in Aspen, Colorado, said, "Korea can play a strong role in expanding nuclear power in the United States." Since the signing of the U.S.-Korea Agreement for Cooperation Concerning Atomic Energy in 1956, South Korea has been strictly limited in uranium enrichment and spent nuclear fuel reprocessing. While the 2015 revision of the agreement codified the possibility of producing low-enriched uranium below 20% with prior consent from the United States, concrete discussions to secure actual authority have been slow. Amid this, a fact sheet issued by President Lee Jae-myung and President Donald Trump last November included related provisions, leading to follow-up bilateral agreements. It is known that the South Korean government has formally requested uranium enrichment authority from the U.S. to promote small modular reactors (SMRs) and stabilize global supply chains. (폰먼은 이날 콜로라도주(州) 애스펀에서 개막한 애스펀안보포럼(ASF) 현장에서 만나 “미국의 원자력 발전 확대에 있어 한국이 강력한 역할을 할 수 있을 것”이라고 했다. 1956년 한미 원자혁협정 체결 이래 한국은 우라늄 농축, 사용후 핵연료 재처리가 엄격히 제한됐다. 2015년 협정을 개정해 미국의 사전 동의(prior consent) 아래 20% 미만의 저농축 우라늄 생산이 가능하도록 명문화했지만, 실제 권한 확보를 위한 구체적 논의는 더딘 상황이다. 이런 가운데 지난해 11월 이재명 대통령과 도널드 트럼프 대통령이 발표한 팩트시트에 관련 내용이 명시돼 양자(兩者) 간 후속 합의가 이뤄지고 있다. 우리 정부가 소형 모듈 원자로(SMR) 육성, 글로벌 공급망 안정을 위해 미국에 우라늄 농축 권한을 공식 요청한 것으로 알려졌다.)

Poneman stated, "Nuclear issues, uranium enrichment and processing are inherently sensitive, and the existence of legal constraints, including the joint declaration on denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula, cannot be avoided," but added, "If the U.S. and Korea proceed step by step carefully and orderly, we could see uranium enrichment taking place in Korea in the future." With the South Korean government committing approximately $350 billion (about 520 trillion won) in investment to the U.S. as a quid pro quo in tariff negotiations, Poneman suggested, "What about Korea investing in U.S. uranium enrichment projects and becoming a business partner? We can learn this business together. The factory is already there, permits have been obtained, and machinery is being built." Poneman noted, "Unfortunately, the United States has lost its domestic uranium enrichment capability," and highlighted the 'fuel cycle' as one of the areas requiring investment. After the Cold War, the U.S. commercial uranium enrichment industry significantly declined, leading to increased dependence on Russian nuclear fuel, but recent substantial investments are being made to rebuild enrichment facilities and restore the supply chain. (폰먼은 “핵 문제, 우라늄 농축·가공이 본질적으로 민감한 문제고 남북 비핵화 공동선언을 포함한 법적 제약이 존재한다는 사실도 피할 수 없다”면서도 “한미가 신중하고 질서 있게 단계를 밟아나간다면 장래에 한국에서 우라늄 농축이 이뤄지는 모습을 볼 수 있을 것”이라고 했다. 우리 정부가 관세 합의 반대급부로 3500억 달러(약 520조원) 대미(對美) 투자를 약정한 가운데, 폰먼은 “한국이 미국의 우라늄 농축 사업에 투자해 비즈니스 파트너가 되는 건 어떠냐”며 “함께 이 사업을 배워나가는 것이다. 이미 공장이 있고, 허가도 받았으며, 기계도 제작하고 있다”고 했다. 폰먼은 “안타깝게도 미국은 자국의 우라늄 농축 능력을 상실해 버렸다”며 투자가 필요한 분야 중 하나로 ‘연료 주기(fuel cycle)’를 꼽았다. 미국은 냉전 후 상업용 우라늄 농축 산업이 크게 쇠퇴해 러시아산 핵연료에 대한 의존도도 높아졌는데, 농축 시설을 다시 짓고 공급망을 복원하는 데 최근 상당한 투자를 하고 있다.)

Regarding some concerns over the safety of nuclear power, Poneman said, "Nuclear energy is one of the safest technologies in the world," noting that "the frequency of accidents is much lower compared to wind and solar power." He added, "Deaths from air pollution amount to millions per year. Nuclear energy is extremely safe and is becoming even safer over time. It will become safer in the future." On SMRs, which are gaining attention as a solution to both AI-era electricity demand and carbon neutrality goals, Poneman expressed, "I am very optimistic about the future. SMRs are not the only solution, but with the explosive increase in demand from data center construction and other factors, we need every source of power we can mobilize." (폰먼은 원자력 발전의 안전성을 우려하는 일부 시각에 대해 “원자력은 세계에서 가장 안전한 기술 중 하나”라며 “사고·발생 빈도를 보면 풍력, 태양광에 비해 훨씬 낮은 수준”이라고 했다. 이어 “대기 오염에 따른 사망자는 매년 수백만 명이나 된다”며 “원자력은 극도로 안전하며 시간이 지날수록 점점 더 안전해지고 있다. 앞으로 더 안전해질 것”이라고 했다. 폰먼은 AI 시대 전력 수요, 탄소중립 목표를 동시에 해결할 대안으로 각광받고 있는 SMR에 대해선 “미래를 매우 낙관한다”며 “SMR이 유일한 해법은 아니지만, 데이터 센터 건설 등으로 폭증하는 수요 규모를 감당하려면 우리가 동원할 수 있는 모든 전력이 필요하다”고 했다.)

Poneman also served as a practitioner who handled North Korean nuclear issues for a long time while working at the White House National Security Council (NSC). During the first North Korean nuclear crisis in 1993-1994, he was in charge of North Korea policy at the Clinton administration's NSC, making him a rare figure with experience in both diplomacy/security and the nuclear industry. Amid widespread perceptions in the U.S. political circles that North Korea's denuclearization has become virtually impossible, Poneman said, "It would have been much easier if China and Russia had cooperated with us from time to time, and if the U.S. and Korea had shown a strong and cooperative attitude as an alliance." However, he stressed, "Recognizing North Korea as a 'nuclear weapon state' is unacceptable. This issue is too important to abandon the goal of eliminating all nuclear weapons." Poneman argued that the Nuclear Consultative Group (NCG) established between the U.S. and Korea under the 2023 Washington Declaration, as well as the U.S. extended deterrence (nuclear umbrella) and security commitments to Korea, must continue to be strengthened. (폰먼은 백악관 국가안보회의(NSC)에 근무하면서 북핵 문제를 오래 다뤄 온 실무자이기도 하다. 1993~1994년 북핵 1차 위기 당시 클린턴 정부 NSC에서 대북 정책을 담당했는데, 외교·안보와 원자력 산업을 모두 경험한 드문 인물인 셈이다. 미 조야(朝野)에 북한 비핵화가 사실상 어려워졌다는 인식이 팽배한 가운데, 폰먼은 “중·러가 때때로 우리와 협력했을 때 한미가 동맹으로서 강하고 협력적인 태도를 보여줬다면 일이 훨씬 더 쉬웠을 것”이라고 했다. 그러면서도 “북한을 ‘핵보유국(nuclear weapon state)’으로 인정하자는 건 용납할 수 없다”며 “이 문제는 너무 중요하기 때문에 모든 핵무기를 제거하겠다는 목표를 포기할 수 없다”고 했다. 폰먼은 2023년 ‘워싱턴 선언’에 따른 한미 간 핵 협의(NCG), 한국에 대한 미국의 확장억제(핵우산)와 안보 공약이 계속해서 강화돼야 한다고 주장했다.)

()

◇ ☞Aspen Institute (◇ ☞애스펀연구소(Aspen Institute))

A non-profit organization founded in 1949 in Aspen, Colorado, by American businessman Walter Paepcke. Paepcke, from Chicago, was inspired by Aspen's natural landscape and conceived the idea of bringing world leaders together for discussions away from their daily routines. Its operational mission is "to solve the most important challenges facing the United States and the world through dialogue and leadership." The Aspen Institute aims to be a nonpartisan convener, stepping back from political structures to facilitate discussions among diverse participants. Programs operate independently in over 30 fields, including economics, education, and the environment. Since 2010, it has hosted the annual 'Aspen Security Forum,' where global diplomacy and security experts gather to discuss domestic and international issues. (미국의 사업가인 월터 펩키가 1949년 콜로라도주 애스펀에 설립한 비영리단체다. 시카고 출신으로 애스펀의 자연경관에 감동한 펩키가 세계의 리더들이 일상에서 벗어나 토론을 하는 아이디어를 구상한 것에서 비롯됐다. “대화와 리더십을 통해 미국과 전 세계가 직면한 가장 중요한 도전 과제들을 해결하겠다”는 것이 운영 취지다. 정치 구도에서 한 발짝 물러나 다양한 사람이 모여서 토론하도록 주선하는 초당적 주관자를 지향한다. 경제·교육·환경 등 30여 분야에서 각 프로그램이 독립적으로 운영되고 있는데, 2010년부터는 매년 전 세계 외교·안보 전문가들이 국내외 문제를 논의하는 ‘애스펀안보포럼’을 개최하고 있다.)

item.title: "Trump Pushes Korea and Japan into Difficult Position to Join Against China... Concerns Over Weak Stance on Taiwan Issue" (“트럼프, 中에 함께 맞설 韓日 어려운 처지 몰아… 대만 문제 약한 모습 우려”)
item.description:
"Trump Pushes Korea and Japan into Difficult Position to Join Against China... Concerns Over Weak Stance on Taiwan Issue" (“트럼프, 中에 함께 맞설 韓日 어려운 처지 몰아… 대만 문제 약한 모습 우려”)

Nicholas Burns, former U.S. ambassador to China, stated on the 15th that President Donald Trump is showing a very weak stance on the Taiwan issue toward Chinese President Xi Jinping, saying, "This is not the time for ambiguity, and I am concerned that President Xi might be judging Trump as a 'weak figure.'" Speaking as a panelist at the China-related session of the Aspen Security Forum (ASF) held in Aspen, Colorado, Burns noted, "In the past 50 years, no U.S. president has negotiated with mainland China over whether to provide defensive weapons to Taiwan," adding, "Saying they are negotiating on the Taiwan issue was a major tactical mistake." (니컬러스 번스 전 중국 주재 미국 대사는 15일 도널드 트럼프 대통령이 시진핑(習近平) 중국 국가주석에게 대만 문제에 있어서 매우 약한 모습을 보이고 있다며 “지금은 애매모호하게 굴 때가 아닌데 시 주석이 트럼프를 ‘약한 인물’로 판단하고 있는 것이 아닌지 우려된다”고 했다. 번스는 이날 콜로라도주(州) 애스펀에서 열린 애스펀안보포럼(ASF)의 중국 관련 세션에 패널로 참석해 “지난 50년 동안 미국의 어떤 대통령도 대만에 방어용 무기를 제공해야 하는지 아닌지를 놓고 중국 본토와 협상한 적이 없다” “대만 문제를 놓고 협상하고 있다고 말한 건 큰 전술적 실수”라며 이같이 밝혔다.)

Trump, shortly after the U.S.-China summit in Beijing last May, caused considerable controversy by describing arms sales to Taiwan as a "bargaining chip" for trade and diplomatic negotiations with China. Amid ongoing tariff negotiations between the U.S. and China, the U.S. government is currently withholding approval for $12 billion (approximately 17.8 trillion won) in arms sales to Taiwan. Burns stated that the U.S. and China will become "fierce competitors in artificial intelligence (AI), quantum supercomputers, synthetic biology, cyberspace, space, and all other fields." He emphasized that China is exerting specific threats to Taiwan as part of its strategic plan, arguing that "this is not the time for ambiguity" and that "casually inserting the Taiwan issue into the list of matters for negotiation with China is an inappropriate approach." He also claimed that while Trump visited China accompanied by major business figures and said he "truly respects President Xi," Xi did not reciprocate this goodwill. (트럼프는 지난 5월 베이징에서 열린 미·중 회담 직후 대만에 대한 무기 판매를 중국과의 무역 및 외교 협상을 위한 ‘협상 카드(chip)’로 표현해 작지 않은 파장이 있었다. 미·중 관세 협상 속 미국 정부는 현재 대만에 대한 120억 달러(약 17조8000억원) 어치 무기 판매 승인을 보류하고 있다. 번스는 미·중이 “인공지능(AI), 양자 슈퍼 컴퓨터, 합성 생물학, 사이버, 우주, 그리고 다른 전 분야에서 치열한 경쟁자(fierce competitors)가 될 것”이라고 했다. 그러면서 중국이 전략적 계획의 일환으로 대만에 구체적인 위협을 행사하고 있어 지금은 애매모호하게 굴 때가 아니라며 “대만 문제를 중국과 협상할 여러 사안들 속 무작정 끼워 넣는 것은 부적절한 태도”라고 지적했다. 트럼프가 주요 기업인을 대동한 채 중국을 방문해 “시 주석을 정말 존경한다”고 했지만, 시 주석이 이런 호의(好意)를 “되돌려주지 않았다”고도 주장했다.)

Burns specifically named allies in the Indo-Pacific region—Japan, South Korea, and India—stating that "high tariffs have put these countries in a more politically difficult position" and that "the U.S. will be strong when it stands with democratic nations on our side in the fierce competition with China, and weak when it does not." Noting that Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba last year raised the possibility of intervention in a Taiwan contingency, escalating the issue into a Japan-China conflict, Burns also pointed out that "the president is silent toward the governments of Japan and the Philippines as they confront Chinese coercion." Elizabeth Economy, a senior fellow at the Hoover Institution who served as an advisor to the U.S. Commerce Department under the Biden administration, remarked, "China retaliated against tariff imposition with a 'strangulation' strategy by leveraging control over critical minerals and rare earths," adding, "We had to step back, and it was a huge strategic mistake because we didn't properly understand the relative trade weight." (번스는 특히 인도·태평양 지역의 동맹국인 일본, 한국, 인도를 호명하며 “높은 관세를 부과해 이들 국가는 정치적으로 더 어려운 처지에 놓이게 됐다”며 “중국과의 치열한 경쟁에서 우리 편에 설 민주주의 국가들과 함께할 때 미국은 강해질 것이고, 그렇지 않을 땐 약해질 것”이라고 했다. 다카이치 사나에 일본 총리가 지난해 11월 대만 유사시 개입 가능성을 언급해 이 문제가 일·중 갈등으로 비화한 가운데, “대통령이 중국의 강압에 맞서는 일본·필리핀 정부에 침묵하고 있다”는 점도 지적했다. 중국 전문가로 바이든 정부에서 상무부 고문을 지낸 엘리자베스 이코노미 후버연구소 선임연구원은 “중국이 핵심 광물, 희토류에 대한 통제권을 활용해 ‘목 조르기’ 전략으로 관세 부과에 반격했다”며 “우리가 한 발 물러서야 했는데 상대적인 무역 비중을 제대로 이해하지 못한 엄청난 전략적 실수였다”고 했다.)

<<> ◇ "Need Cooperation with Allies Like Korea, Key in Memory Sector" ()

Tarun Chhabra, head of national security policy linking government and the AI industry at the AI company Anthropic, stated, "Whether the U.S. can maintain an edge over China depends on whether it can sustain strong export controls," adding, "This requires cooperation with allies like Japan, the Netherlands, and key players in the memory sector such as South Korea and Taiwan." Chhabra, who also served as a senior advisor for technology and national security at the White House National Security Council (NSC) under the Biden administration, designed key policies. He argued, "Almost all major Chinese research institutes are engaged in 'adversarial distillation,' extracting intellectual property, coding, and agent capabilities from Anthropic and our U.S. competitors' models," and that "if we can prevent this, the current technological gap of about 6 to 9 months could widen to 12 to 18 months." (◇ “메모리 핵심인 한국 같은 동맹과 협력 필요”)

<<> ◇ ☞Aspen Institute (인공지능(AI) 기업 앤스로픽에서 정부와 AI 산업을 연결하는 국가 안보 정책을 총괄하고 있는 타룬 차브라 헤드는 “미국이 중국에 우위를 유지할 수 있냐는 강력한 수출 통제를 지속할 수 있을지에 달려 있다”며 “이를 위해 일본·네덜란드, 메모리 분야에서 핵심 역할을 하는 한국·대만 같은 동맹과의 협력이 필요하다”고 했다. 차브라는 바이든 정부 백악관 국가안보회의(NSC)에서 기술·국가안보 담당 선임보좌관으로 있으면서 주요 정책을 설계한 인물이다. 그는 “중국의 거의 모든 주요 연구소가 앤스로픽뿐 아니라 미국 경쟁사 모델에서 지적재산권, 코딩·에이전트 능력 등을 추출하는 ‘적대적 추출(adversarial distillation)’을 진행하고 있다”며 “이를 막을 수 있다면 현재 6~9개월 정도 하는 기술적 격차가 12~18개월 정도로 늘어날 수 있다”고 주장했다.)

The Aspen Institute is a non-profit organization founded in 1949 by American businessman Walter Paepcke in Aspen, Colorado. Inspired by the natural landscape of Aspen, the Chicago native conceived the idea of bringing together world leaders for discussions away from their daily routines. Its mission is "to solve the most important challenges facing the U.S. and the world through dialogue and leadership." The institute aims to be a nonpartisan facilitator, stepping back from political divisions to bring diverse people together for discussion. Programs operate independently across more than 30 fields, including economics, education, and the environment. Since 2010, it has annually hosted the 'Aspen Security Forum,' where global diplomatic and security experts discuss domestic and international issues. ()

item.title: Top North Korean and Chinese Party Officials Hold Talks in Pyongyang: “Promote DPRK-China Relations to a Higher Level” (北·中 당 최고위 간부 평양서 회담 “북중 관계 높은 단계로 추동”)
item.description:
Top North Korean and Chinese Party Officials Hold Talks in Pyongyang: “Promote DPRK-China Relations to a Higher Level” (北·中 당 최고위 간부 평양서 회담 “북중 관계 높은 단계로 추동”)

North Korean Workers’ Party Central Committee Secretary Jo Yong-won met with Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) Chairman Wang Huning, who visited North Korea on the occasion of the 65th anniversary of the DPRK-China friendship treaty, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported on the 16th. Chairman Wang is ranked fourth in the Chinese Communist Party, following General Secretary Xi Jinping, Premier Li Keqiang, National People’s Congress Standing Committee Chairman Li Zhanshu, and CPPCC National Committee Chairman Wang Yang. (북한 조용원 노동당 중앙위원회 비서가 북·중 우호 조약 체결 65주년을 계기로 북한을 찾은 중국 왕후닝 전국인민정치협상회의(정협) 주석과 회담했다고 조선중앙통신이 16일 보도했다. 왕 주석은 중국공산당에서 시진핑 총서기, 리커창 국무원 총리, 리잔수 전국인민대표대회 상무위원장, 왕양 정협 전국위원회 주석에 이어 서열 4위이다.)

According to the news agency, a Chinese Communist Party and government delegation led by Chairman Wang made an official friendly visit to North Korea the previous day at the invitation of the Workers’ Party of Korea and the government. Kim Hyong-sik, Vice Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Supreme People’s Assembly of North Korea, welcomed the Chinese delegation at Pyongyang International Airport. The Chinese delegation laid a wreath at the DPRK-China Friendship Tower, bearing the inscription: “The martyrs of the Chinese People’s Volunteers (Chinese troops who fought on North Korea’s side during the 6.25 War) will be immortal.” (통신에 따르면, 왕 주석을 단장으로 하는 중국공산당 및 정부 대표단이 북한 노동당과 정부의 초청에 따라 전날 북한을 공식 친선 방문했다. 김형식 북한 최고인민회의 상임위원회 부위원장 등이 평양국제비행장에서 중국 대표단을 맞이했다. 중국 대표단은 조·중(북·중) 우의탑에 “중국인민지원군(6·25전쟁에서 북한 편을 들어 참전한 중국군) 열사들은 영생불멸할 것이다”라는 글이 적혀 있는 꽃바구니를 진정했다.)

During a meeting held at the Mansudae Assembly Hall in Pyongyang, Jo Yong-won stated: “The rapidly changing current international political situation demands that the two countries, in accordance with the fundamental spirit of the Treaty on Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance between the DPRK and China (the DPRK-China Friendship Treaty), further strengthen combat unity and support solidarity for the victorious advance of the common socialist cause, and continuously deepen and develop friendly cooperative relations for the sake of the victorious advancement of the joint socialist cause.” (이어 평양의사당에서 열린 회담에서 조용원은 “격변하는 현 국제 정치 정세는 두 나라가 조·중 우호·협조 및 호상(상호) 원조에 관한 조약(북·중 우호 조약)의 근본 정신에 맞게 공동의 사회주의 위업의 승리적 전진을 위해 전투적 단결과 지지 연대를 더욱 강화해 친선 협조 관계를 부단히 심화·발전시켜 나갈 것을 요구하고 있다”고 했다.)

He added: “Under the direct attention and wise leadership of Comrade Kim Jong-un and Comrade Xi [Jinping], the DPRK-China friendly relations are entering a new phase of vitality in their development,” and proposed: “Let us closely strengthen strategic communication and tactical cooperation between the two parties and two countries, expanding and developing bilateral relations in diverse directions.” (이어 “김정은 동지와 시 동지의 직접적인 관심과 현명한 영도 밑에 조·중(북·중) 친선 관계는 자기 발전의 새로운 활력기를 맞이하고 있다”며 “두 당, 두 나라 사이의 전략적 의사소통과 전술적 협력을 긴밀히 해 쌍무 관계를 다방면적으로 확대·발전시켜 나가자”고 했다.)

Chairman Wang responded: “The signing of the friendship treaty established a legal foundation to consolidate the blood-sealed combat friendship,” and noted: “Grandly commemorating the 65th anniversary of the treaty’s signing is an important shared understanding of the supreme leaders of both parties and countries.” (왕 주석은 “우호 조약이 체결돼 피로써 맺어진 전투적 우의를 공고히 할 수 있는 법률적 기초가 마련됐다”며 “조약 체결 65돌을 성대히 기념하는 것은 두 당, 두 나라 최고 영도자들의 중요한 공동 인식”이라고 화답했다.)

He further stated: “We intend to take as a fundamental guideline the important agreements reached during the historic Pyongyang summit of the supreme leaders of both parties and countries, which opened a beautiful chapter in traditional China-DPRK friendship and injected strong momentum, and to propel China-DPRK relations to a higher level.” (이어 “전통적인 중·조(중·북) 친선의 아름다운 장을 펼치고 강력한 동력을 주입한 두 당, 두 나라 최고 영도자들의 역사적인 평양 상봉에서 이룩된 중요 합의를 근본 지침으로 삼고, 중·조 관계를 보다 높은 단계로 추동해 나가고자 한다”고 했다.)

The news agency reported that the meeting was “conducted in a comradely and friendly atmosphere” and that “issues were discussed regarding strengthening party exchanges between the two parties and countries, deepening cooperation in various fields including economy and culture, and promoting the welfare of the peoples of both countries.” (통신은 회담이 “동지적이며 친선적인 분위기 속에서 진행됐다”며 “두 당, 두 나라 사이의 당적 교류를 강화하고, 경제와 문화를 비롯한 여러 분야에서의 협조를 심화시켜 양국 인민의 복리를 증진시키기 위한 문제들이 토의됐다”고 전했다.)

Attending the meeting from the North Korean side were Kim Hyong-sik, Vice Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Supreme People’s Assembly; Mun Song-hyok, Deputy Department Director of the Workers’ Party; Kim Myong-su, Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs; and Kang Chol-ho, Vice Minister of Urban Management. From the Chinese side were Wang Dongfeng, Vice Chairman of the CPPCC; Liu Jianchao, Minister of the International Department of the Chinese Communist Party; Qi Yu, Secretary of the Party Committee of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Pei Jinjia, Minister of the Ministry of Veterans Affairs; and Wang Yajun, Chinese Ambassador to North Korea. (회담에는 북한 측에서는 김형식 최고인민회의 상임위원회 부위원장, 문성혁 노동당 부부장, 김명수 외무성 부상, 강철호 도시경영성 부상이 배석했다. 중국 측에서는 왕둥펑 정협 부주석, 류하이싱 중국공산당 대외연락부장, 치위 외교부 당위원회 서기, 페이진자 퇴역군인사업부장, 왕야쥔 주북 중국대사 등이 배석했다.)

item.title: Park Jie-won: "Yoo Si-min, you harassed DJ for 5 years too... Stop shaking President Lee" (박지원 “유시민, DJ도 5년 괴롭히더니... 李대통령 흔들기 멈추라”)
item.description:
Park Jie-won: "Yoo Si-min, you harassed DJ for 5 years too... Stop shaking President Lee" (박지원 “유시민, DJ도 5년 괴롭히더니... 李대통령 흔들기 멈추라”)

Park Jie-won, a lawmaker of the Democratic Party of Korea, responded to Yoo Si-min's remarks that "President Lee Jae-myung's path will end in failure" by saying, "Stop shaking President Lee." (박지원 더불어민주당 의원이 “이재명 대통령의 노선은 실패로 끝날 것”이라고 발언한 유시민씨 발언을 두고 “이 대통령 흔들기를 멈추라”고 했다.)

Park, a former chief of staff to the late President Kim Dae-jung, wrote on Facebook on the 16th, "I couldn't sleep. I only slept 2 hours," adding, "Former Chairman Yoo also shook the DJ (Kim Dae-jung) government for all five years in the past. As a clearly progressive intellectual, who does writer Yoo Si-min have as an alternative as he now shakes President Lee Jae-myung, who has only been in office for just over a year?" (김대중 전 대통령 비서실장을 지낸 박 의원은 16일 페이스북에서 “잠을 설친다. 2시간 잤다”며 “유 전 이사장은 과거에도 DJ(김대중) 정부를 5년 내내 흔들었다. 분명 진보적 지식인인 유시민 작가는 누구를 대안으로 두고 이제 (취임한 지) 갓 1년지난 이재명 대통령을 흔들어댈까”라고 했다.)

The previous day, Yoo appeared on the pro-government YouTube channel "Maebul Show" and said about President Lee Jae-myung's "prosecutor reform" and state management, "He is making very wrong judgments," and "He is heading down an inevitable path to failure." (전날 유씨는 친여 유튜브 매불쇼에 출연해 이재명 대통령의 ‘검찰 개혁’과 정국 운영에 대해 “매우 잘못된 판단을 하고 있다”며 “필연적인 실패의 길로 가고 있다”고 했었다.)

In response, Park said, "(Yoo) supported his (Seoul National University) mentor, conservative party candidate Cho Soon, and advocated the famous 'DJ will fail theory,' but the people chose DJ." The 'DJ will fail theory' refers to Yoo's opposition to former President Kim becoming a presidential candidate in the book 'The Rules of the 97 Presidential Election Game,' published ahead of the 15th presidential election in 1997, based on 'anti-Honam sentiment.' (이에 대해 박 의원은 “(유씨는) 그의 (서울대) 은사인 보수정당 조순 후보를 지지하며 그 유명한 ‘DJ필패론’을 역설했지만 국민은 DJ를 선택했다”고 했다. ’DJ 필패론’은 유씨가 1997년 15대 대선을 앞두고 출간한 ’97 대선 게임의 법칙’이라는 책에서 ‘반(反) 호남 정서’를 근거로 김 전 대통령이 대권 후보가 되는 것에 반대했던 것을 말한다.)

Park said, "(Yoo) shook and harassed the DJ government for all five years," adding, "Despite his malice and sabotage, DJ was recorded as the most historically and nationally successful president." (박 의원은 “(유씨는) DJ 정부를 5년 내내 흔들고 괴롭혔다”며 “그의 패악질과 훼방에도 DJ는 역사적 국민적 가장 성공한 대통령으로 기록됐다”고 했다.)

He continued, "President Lee is also heading not toward an inevitable path to failure despite his baseless shaking, but toward an inevitable path to success," adding, "In his first year in power, he restored democracy, and the three major reforms to clean up the insurrection are progressing successfully. The '345 policy vision' has the entire nation holding hope and making efforts." (그러면서 “이 대통령도 그의 이유 없는 흔들림에도 필연적 실패의 길이 아니라 필연적 성공의 길로 가고 있다”며 “집권 1년 차에 민주주의를 회복시켰고 내란청산 3대 개혁은 성공적으로 진행되고 있다.‘345정책 비전’은 온 국민이 희망을 갖고 노력한다”고 했다.)

Park also said, "(Yoo) once said that after age 60, the brain rots. Now writer Yoo will soon enter his 70s, won't he?" He added, "Harassing DJ for five years should be enough. Helping President Lee to walk the path of inevitable success will prevent insurrectionist forces from emerging. Please help." (박 의원은 “(유씨는) 60세가 넘으면 뇌가 (썩는다고) 운운했다. 이제 유 작가도 머잖아 70대에 진입하지 않느냐”고도 했다. 이어 “DJ 5년을 괴롭혔으면 그것으로 충분하다. 이 대통령을 도와 필연적 성공의 길로 가야 내란세력이 등장 못한다. 도와 달라”고 했다.)

Reactions from the ruling camp to Yoo's remarks have been heated. Minister of Economy and Finance Park Hong-geun wrote on Facebook the previous day, "I cannot contain my lament over (Yoo's) remarks," adding, "It is hard to believe this is the language of a comrade who acted as a nerve tonic for the people and braved the cold, dark winter nights of the insurrection martial law together, which seemed endless." He continued, "This kind of criticism is no different from a curse. It appears not as concern, but as a wish. Why keep sowing seeds of division?" (유씨 발언을 두고 여권에선 격앙된 반응이 이어지고 있다. 박홍근 기획예산처 장관은 전날 페이스북에서 “(유씨) 발언에 개탄을 금할 수 없다”며 “국민의 신경안정제 노릇을 하며, 끝나지 않을 것만 같던 내란 계엄의 춥고 어두운 겨울밤을 함께 헤쳐온 동지의 언어라고는 믿기 어렵다”고 했다. 이어 “이런 식의 비난은 저주와 다르지 않다. 걱정이 아니라 소망으로 비칠 뿐이다. 왜 자꾸 분열의 씨앗을 뿌리는가”라고 했다.)

item.title: Yoon Sang-hyun, Chairman of the Special Committee for National Audit on Election Commission, "Recount and Special Counsel Must Go Together" (윤상현 선관위 국조특위 위원장 “재검표·특검 함께 가야”)
item.description:
Yoon Sang-hyun, Chairman of the Special Committee for National Audit on Election Commission, "Recount and Special Counsel Must Go Together" (윤상현 선관위 국조특위 위원장 “재검표·특검 함께 가야”)

Yoon Sang-hyun, a lawmaker from the People Power Party and chairman of the National Assembly's Special Committee for a National Audit on the June 3 Local Election Ballot Shortage Incident, demanded on the 16th that the Democratic Party of Korea accept both a recount and a special counsel investigation. (국회 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태 국정조사 특별위원회 위원장인 윤상현 국민의힘 의원은 16일 더불어민주당에 재검표와 특검을 모두 수용하라고 요구했다.)

In a Facebook post that morning, Rep. Yoon stated, "Although over a month has passed since the June 3 local elections, the public's doubts regarding the infringement of voting rights, such as the ballot shortage, have still not been resolved." He further criticized, "The debate continues to focus on methodology rather than uncovering the truth that the public desires." (윤 의원은 이날 오전 페이스북에 글을 올려 “6·3 지방선거 이후 한 달이 훌쩍 지났지만 투표용지 부족 등 참정권 훼손 사태에 대한 국민적 의구심은 여전히 해소되지 않았다”고 주장했다. 그러면서 “국민이 원하는 진실 규명보다 방법론을 둘러싼 논쟁만 이어지고 있다”고 비판했다.)

Rep. Yoon continued, "A recount and a special counsel are not a matter of choice," distinguishing them by saying, "A public recount is a process of verifying the facts before the people, while a special counsel is a process to establish responsibility according to the law and principles." He asserted, "These two procedures are not a choice but are complementary to each other." (윤 의원은 이어 “재검표와 특검은 선택의 대상이 아니다”라며 “공개 재검표는 국민 앞에서 사실을 검증하는 절차이고, 특검은 법과 원칙에 따라 책임을 규명하는 절차”라고 구분했다. 그러면서 “두 절차는 선택의 문제가 아니라 서로를 보완하는 관계”라고 주장했다.)

Rep. Yoon stated, "Time does not resolve suspicions," and "Only transparent verification can dispel doubts, and only a thorough investigation can reveal responsibility." He added, "A public recount and a special counsel must go together. That is the way to restore the people's voting rights and regain trust in South Korea's elections." (윤 의원은 “의혹은 시간이 해결해 주지 않는다”며 “투명한 검증만이 의혹을 해소하고, 철저한 수사만이 책임을 밝힐 수 있다”며 “공개 재검표와 특검은 함께 가야 한다. 그것이 국민의 참정권을 회복하고 대한민국 선거에 대한 신뢰를 되찾는 길”이라고 했다.)

Previously, on the 14th, the ruling and opposition parties discussed a public recount of the 2.47 million ballots stored at the Jamsil Olympic Park in Songpa-gu, Seoul, and the adoption of a resolution calling for a special counsel investigation into the infringement of public voting rights during a hearing of the special committee held at the National Assembly. (앞서 지난 14일 여야는 국회에서 열린 국조특위 청문회에서 서울 송파구 잠실 올림픽공원에 보관된 투표지 247만장에 대한 공개 재검표와 국민 참정권 침해 사태에 대한 특검 촉구 결의안 채택 등을 논의했다.)

However, the Democratic Party maintained a stance of conducting a recount first, while the People Power Party insisted on proceeding with both the recount and the special counsel simultaneously, showing a difference in positions. The special committee plans to hold a second hearing on the 22nd to further discuss the recount and the adoption of a resolution calling for a special counsel. (그러나 민주당은 재검표를 먼저 하자는 입장인 반면, 국민의힘은 재검표와 특검을 동시에 진행해야 한다는 입장으로 서로 차이를 보였다. 국조특위는 오는 22일 두 번째로 청문회를 하고 재검표와 특검 촉구 결의안 채택을 다시 논의할 예정이다.)

item.title: Controversial Unified Military Academy for Army, Navy, and Air Force... Ruling Party and Government Decide to Establish in Daejeon's Jaundae (논란의 육해공 통합 사관학교... 당정, 대전 자운대에 창설키로)
item.description:
Controversial Unified Military Academy for Army, Navy, and Air Force... Ruling Party and Government Decide to Establish in Daejeon's Jaundae (논란의 육해공 통합 사관학교... 당정, 대전 자운대에 창설키로)

The Democratic Party of Korea and the government announced on the 16th that they have decided to establish a four-year national military academy, integrating the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies, in Daejeon's Jaundae area. The ruling party and government discussed specific measures for this during a consultation on the establishment of the national military academy held at the National Assembly on the same day. (더불어민주당과 정부는 16일 육·해·공군 사관학교를 통합한 4년제 국군사관학교를 대전 자운대에 창설하기로 했다고 밝혔다. 당정은 이날 국회에서 열린 국군사관학교 창설 당정 협의에서 이를 위한 구체적인 방안을 논의했다.)

After the consultation ended on the same day, Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek stated, "Military academies have been the cradle of elite officers and the stronghold of national defense for the past several decades. However, various opinions have been raised about whether today's military academies are still fulfilling their functions and roles as top-notch officer education institutions." He added, "It is time for us to answer for ourselves the questions of whether our military can win in the future and whether becoming an officer can be a thrilling choice for future generations of talent." He further noted, "The newly established National Military Academy, to be located in the Daejeon Jaundae area, will cultivate officers equipped with creative and convergent thinking, expertise, and technological sensitivity." <<> Earlier in the consultation, Democratic Party acting leader and floor leader Han Byung-do said, "Now we must focus on cultivating integrated commanders capable of competently conducting multi-domain operations, nurturing hexagonal talents." He lamented, "Unfortunately, the individual Army, Navy, and Air Force academies have faced several limitations." <<> Representative Han stated, "The establishment of a National Military Academy to cultivate capable integrated talents and future defense leaders who will lead a smart strong military is an urgent task that cannot be postponed." He assured, "The party will spare no support to ensure the National Military Academy transforms into a world-class elite military academy." <<> Democratic Party Policy Committee Chairperson Han Jeong-ae said, "The integration of the separate service academies is a long-attempted but delayed reform." She added, "Discussions on integrating the service academies began with the Kim Young-sam administration, and various integration plans were discussed during the Roh Moo-hyun administration in connection with the future population decline." <<> Regarding public opposition to the integration of military academies, Chairperson Han Jeong-ae stated, "It disparages the military's future blueprint to robustly and resolutely safeguard national security amidst the rapidly changing world order." She added, "We will invest large-scale budgets, including securing top-tier faculty and cutting-edge facilities." <<> Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek said, "As the first civilian defense minister in 64 years, I never expected defense reform to be smooth, but I also never thought it impossible." He asserted, "I will not hesitate or look left and right, but will see defense reform through to completion." (안규백 국방장관은 이날 협의가 끝난 뒤 “사관학교는 지난 수십년간 국군정예장교 산실이자 호국강성 요람이었다. 그러나 오늘날 사관학교가 여전히 최고 장교 교육 기관으로 기능과 역할 다하고 있는지 대해서는 다양한 의견 제기되고 있다”며 “우리 군이 미래에도 승리할 수 있는가 장교들이 미래 세대 인재들에게 가슴 뛰는 선택 될 수 있는가 질문에 우리 스스로 답해야 할 시점”이라고 했다. 이어 “새롭게 출범할 국군사관학교는 대전 자운대 지역에 유치해 창의적, 융합적 사고와 전문성, 기술 감수성 등이 구비된 장교를 양성해 나갈 것”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Opposition Party: “DP, Wasting Taxpayer Money on Endless Special Counsel Extensions,” “Is This a Permanent Political Retaliation Body?” (野 “민주, 혈세 펑펑 특검 연장” “정치보복 상설기구인가”)
item.description:
Opposition Party: “DP, Wasting Taxpayer Money on Endless Special Counsel Extensions,” “Is This a Permanent Political Retaliation Body?” (野 “민주, 혈세 펑펑 특검 연장” “정치보복 상설기구인가”)

The People Power Party (PPP) has pushed back against the Democratic Party (DP) for unilaterally extending the investigation period of the Second Comprehensive Special Counsel (Special Counsel Kwon Chang-young), calling it a “permanent political retaliation body.” The Second Comprehensive Special Counsel is tasked with investigating aspects overlooked in the three major special counsel probes—dealing with the insurrection, Kim Keon-hee, and the Marine who died in the line of duty—along with newly raised suspicions. <<> PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk stated at a party meeting on the 16th, “The DP is recklessly spending taxpayer money on special counsel investigations that yield no results, pushing forward with the three major special counsels, a second special counsel, and now even an extension.” He added, “On the same day the DP unilaterally passed the extension law for the Second Comprehensive Special Counsel in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, they astonishingly conducted a raid on former Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport Won Hee-ryong. They’ve been investigating for over a year and imposed a travel ban, yet they’ve failed to prove any charges and have achieved nothing so far.” <<> Earlier, floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik also remarked, “Combining the 510-day investigation period of the first three major special counsels, the 150-day period of the Second Comprehensive Special Counsel, and this additional 30-day extension totals 690 days. Is it normal for a special counsel to operate for two years?” He further questioned, “Extending again and again, how much longer will they drag out the investigation period? Why not just amend the special counsel’s deadline to ‘until President Lee Jae-myung leaves office’?” <<> Secretary-General Jeong Hee-yong stated, “The DP’s move to change the law to extend the investigation period is tantamount to turning the special counsel, an exceptional and temporary body, into a permanent political retaliation institution.” PPP lawmaker Shin Seong-beom also expressed frustration, saying, “It’s been a year and seven months since the martial law incident, yet we’re still dealing with insurrection, special counsels, special special counsels, and comprehensive special counsels—how frustrating.” <<> Despite the absence of PPP lawmakers, the DP unilaterally passed a revised special counsel bill in the National Assembly’s Legislation and Judiciary Committee plenary session the previous day, extending the investigation period of the Second Comprehensive Special Counsel by one month. The revision increases the number of dispatched public officials from 130 to 150 and adds the Ministry of National Defense to the list of agencies that can be requested to dispatch personnel. It also includes a provision that among special investigators with at least five years of legal experience, a public prosecutor can be designated to handle the trial proceedings of cases indicted by the special counsel. Matters where the Second Comprehensive Special Counsel could overturn decisions of the previous three major special counsels or affect the maintenance of prosecution are required to be consulted with the respective special counsel. <<> The revision adds ‘obstruction of audit’ to the list of investigation targets. The special counsel is currently investigating suspicions surrounding the relocation of former President Yoon Suk-yeol’s office and residence. The DP has argued that the Board of Audit and Inspection covered up the case through a negligent audit. Observers in the legal community suggest that the special counsel may have begun investigating the audit agency’s case first and then supplemented the legal basis through this legislative amendment. <<> In response, PPP spokesperson Park Seong-hoon criticized, “This is an endless special counsel aimed at oppressing the opposition, a legislative rampage by the DP that shakes the rule of law.” He continued, “Changing the law like a referee altering rules mid-game because the DP didn’t get the conclusion it wanted is a direct challenge to the rule of law. It represents wielding the law for the convenience of power and undermines the very reason for and foundation of the special counsel system.” (국민의힘은 더불어민주당이 2차 종합특검(특별검사 권창영)의 수사 기간을 일방적으로 연장한 데 대해 “정치 보복 상설 기구”라고 반발했다. 2차 종합특검은 내란·김건희·순직 해병 등 3대 특검 수사에서 미진한 부분과 새롭게 제기된 의혹을 수사하는 특검이다.)

item.title: Ahn Cheol-soo: "President Lee, Is Oh Se-hoon a Screen? ... Stop the Theater at Cabinet Meetings" (안철수 “李대통령, 오세훈이 병풍이냐… 국무회의 연극 중단해야”)
item.description:
Ahn Cheol-soo: "President Lee, Is Oh Se-hoon a Screen? ... Stop the Theater at Cabinet Meetings" (안철수 “李대통령, 오세훈이 병풍이냐… 국무회의 연극 중단해야”)

Ahn Cheol-soo, a lawmaker from the People Power Party, said on the 16th regarding the incident on the 14th when President Lee Jae-myung and Prime Minister Han Sung-sook silenced Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon's remarks on real estate policy during a cabinet meeting, "Is Mayor Oh a screen?" and demanded, "Apologize to the 10 million citizens of Seoul." (안철수 국민의힘 의원은 지난 14일 이재명 대통령과 한성숙 국무총리가 국무회의에서 부동산 정책에 대한 오세훈 서울시장의 발언을 제지한 데 대해 16일 “오 시장이 병풍이냐”며 “1000만 서울시민에게 사과하라”고 했다.)

In a Facebook post that morning, Ahn wrote, "If you weren't going to give Mayor Oh a chance to speak at all, why did you seat the representative of 10 million Seoul citizens there? Was it to have a screen in front of the live broadcast cameras?" He added, "Treating him like an ugly duckling and bullying him—you must find it amusing." (안 의원은 이날 오전 페이스북에 글을 올려 “오 시장은 발언 기회조차 주지 않을 거면서 1000만 서울시민의 대표를 왜 앉혀놓았느냐”며 “생중계 카메라 앞 병풍이 필요했던 것이냐”고 했다. “(오 시장을) 미운 오리 새끼 취급하며 ‘이지메(집단 괴롭힘)’를 놓으니 유쾌하나 보다”고도 했다.)

Ahn pointed out, "You put 'gathering public opinion' on the agenda, claiming to listen to the public sentiment on real estate, but then blocked the mouth of the Seoul mayor, who is on the front lines of the real estate issue." Referring to Prime Minister Han's action of stopping Mayor Oh and telling him to submit his opinions in writing, he said, "If the government slaps down even the Seoul mayor's voice to a document like this, how can it possibly listen to the voices of the people?" (안 의원은 “부동산 민심을 듣겠다며 ‘국민 의견 수렴’을 안건으로 올려놓고, 정작 부동산 문제의 최전선에 선 서울시장의 입은 막았다”고 했다. 이어 한 총리가 오 시장의 발언을 막으며 의견을 서면으로 내라고 한 것을 거론하면서 “이렇게 서울시장의 육성도 서류로 후려치는 정부가 국민 목소리는 어떻게 듣겠느냐”고 했다.)

Ahn questioned, "Is this retaliation for the defeat of candidate Jung Won-oh, whom President Lee endorsed (the Democratic Party candidate for Seoul mayor in the June 3 local elections)?" He added, "If it were 'Mayor Jung Won-oh,' would you have snapped at him to submit it in writing and speak later?" (안 의원은 “이 대통령이 찍었던 정원오 후보(6·3 지방선거 서울시장 선거 민주당 후보)의 낙선에 대한 보복이냐”며 “만약 ‘정원오 서울시장’이었어도 문서로 제출하고 나중에 말하라며 면박을 주었겠느냐”고 했다.)

Ahn further noted, "Moreover, President Lee, as a former Gyeonggi governor, knows how important it is to convey local voices to the central government. Yet, despite that, this act can only be seen as intentional." (안 의원은 “더구나 이 대통령은 경기지사 출신으로, 중앙에 지역의 목소리를 전달하는 게 얼마나 중요한지 아는 사람”이라며 “그럼에도 이런 행위를 한 것은 의도적이라고밖에 볼 수 없다”고도 짚었다.)

Ahn stated, "We must stop holding cabinet meetings where these president-worshipers gather, flatter each other, laugh, and chatter." He also said, "We should not even broadcast them—it's a waste of airwaves and a absurd play funded by taxpayers." He added, "President Lee must apologize to the 10 million citizens of Seoul and put an end to this theater disguised as a cabinet meeting." item.title: Han Dong-hoon Rejects Ahn Cheol-soo's 'Form a New Party' Suggestion, Says 'Many Sympathize with Conservative Reconstruction' (한동훈, 안철수 ‘창당 권유’ 일축 “많은 분이 보수 재건에 공감”)
item.description:
Han Dong-hoon Rejects Ahn Cheol-soo's 'Form a New Party' Suggestion, Says 'Many Sympathize with Conservative Reconstruction' (한동훈, 안철수 ‘창당 권유’ 일축 “많은 분이 보수 재건에 공감”)

Independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon on the 16th reiterated his intent to rejoin the People Power Party (PPP), responding to fellow PPP lawmaker Ahn Cheol-soo's opposition to his reinstatement and suggestion to form a new party, stating, "I have indicated that I am returning." (무소속 한동훈 의원은 16일 국민의힘 안철수 의원이 한 의원 복당을 반대하며 창당하라고 언급한 데 대해 “제가 돌아간다고 말씀드렸다”면서 복당 의사를 거듭 밝혔다.)

When asked by reporters at the National Assembly about Ahn's 'suggestion to form a new party,' Han countered, "Is he the one planning to form a party?" He added, "The conservative reconstruction I speak of involves a landslide victory in the 2028 (general election) and reclaiming power in 2030," and "I feel that many people are sympathetic to that path." <<> Regarding PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk's remarks that there is no justification for Han's reinstatement, Han said, "He likely wants to pick a fight with me somehow to prolong his own political survival." Earlier, in a YouTube interview with Pen and Mike, Jang had opposed Han's reinstatement, stating, "He wants to remain the person who prevented martial law and led the impeachment, while pushing Choo Kyung-ho, Daegu Mayor, and the PPP into a corner—then suddenly he wants to rejoin the PPP? What kind of logic is that?" (한 의원은 이날 국회에서 기자들과 만나 안 의원의 ‘창당 권유’와 관련한 질문에 “본인이 창당하신대요?”라고 반문했다. 이어 “제가 말한 보수 재건은 2028년 (총선) 압승과 2030년 정권 탈환”이라며 “많은 분이 그 길에 공감하고 계신다는 걸 느낀다”고 했다.)

Han said, "Whatever he says, I'm not sure it's worth my response." He continued, "This is a highly significant part of the past and history, but I will not dwell on it. I will look toward the future of conservative reconstruction and victory. I will stand with everyone who shares that vision." Han also added, "I see that the number of people opposing (my reinstatement) out of personal greed is decreasing." (국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 ‘한 의원의 복당 명분이 없다’는 취지로 언급한 데 대해서는 “그분이 저한테 어떻게든 싸움을 걸어서 연명해보고 싶은 것 아니겠나”고 했다. 앞서 장 대표는 전날 펜앤마이크 유튜브 인터뷰에서 한 의원 복당 문제에 대해 “자신은 계엄을 막고 탄핵을 주도한 사람으로 남고, 추경호 대구시장과 국민의힘은 사지로 몰아넣고 갑자기 국민의힘에 복당하겠다는 게 도대체 무슨 논리냐”며 반대한다는 입장을 거듭 밝혔다.)

On the morning of the same day, Han attended a seminar of the 'National Assembly Global Diplomacy and Security Forum' held at the National Assembly Members' Office Building. Although Jang Dong-hyuk is also a member of the forum, he left the group's Telegram chatroom after Han was invited to join last month and also did not attend the seminar. (한 의원은 “뭐라고 말하든 제가 대꾸할 필요가 있을지 모르겠다”며 “대단히 중요한 과거이고 역사인데, 저는 거기에 집착하지 않고 미래의 보수 재건과 승리를 바라보겠다. 거기에 공감하는 모든 분과 함께하겠다”고 했다. 한 의원은 “사적 욕심을 채우기 위해 (복당을) 반대하는 사람 숫자가 줄어들고 있다고 본다”고도 했다.)

Attendees of the lecture included PPP lawmakers Yun Jae-ok, the forum's representative, and Kim Gun, the research chair, along with Kim Jung-jae, Cho Eun-hee, Kang Myung-goo, Kang Sun-young, Seo Ji-young, Yoo Yong-won, Lee Dal-hee, and Han Ji-ah, as well as Reform Party lawmaker Lee Joo-young. (한 대표는 이날 오전 국회 의원회관에서 열린 ‘국회 글로벌외교안보포럼’ 세미나에 참석했다. 장동혁 대표도 포럼 회원이지만 지난달 한 의원이 가입하며 단체 텔레그램 대화방에 초대되자 채팅방을 나갔고, 이날 세미나에도 불참했다.)

item.title: Han Byung-do: "People Power Party, Cooperate on Assembly Organization and Bills... If Ignored, We Will Make a Stern Decision" (한병도 “국힘, 원 구성·법안 처리 협조하라… 외면하면 엄중 결단”)
item.description:
Han Byung-do: "People Power Party, Cooperate on Assembly Organization and Bills... If Ignored, We Will Make a Stern Decision" (한병도 “국힘, 원 구성·법안 처리 협조하라… 외면하면 엄중 결단”)

Han Byung-do, acting leader and floor leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, stated on the 16th that if the People Power Party does not cooperate in forming the standing committees for the second half of the 22nd National Assembly, "we will have no choice but to make a stern decision." This effectively pressures the People Power Party, suggesting that the Democratic Party could take all standing committee chairperson positions. <<> At a party policy coordination meeting held at the National Assembly that morning, Acting Leader Han said, "The Assembly has come to a halt due to the irresponsible foot-dragging of the People Power Party, and we are deeply sorry to the people." He added, "Due to the meaningless boycott by the People Power Party, 59 livelihood bills, the Election Commission special counsel law, and follow-up legislation for the three mega projects are all stalled." <<> Han then said, "Nevertheless, the People Power Party is making the audacious claim that the Democratic Party is threatening and stalling for time," adding, "The people already know full well who is stopping the Assembly and holding livelihoods hostage." <<> Han urged, "The People Power Party should immediately return to the Assembly to finalize its organization and cooperate in processing livelihood bills," and warned, "I repeat my warning. If the People Power Party continues to turn its back on the people’s livelihoods, the Democratic Party will have no choice but to make a stern decision." <<> The Democratic Party and the People Power Party attempted to negotiate the distribution of standing committee chairpersons for the second half of the Assembly on the 22nd of last month, but the talks broke down due to a failure to narrow differences over who would take the chairmanship of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee. The People Power Party argues that the opposition party should take the Judiciary Committee chair to prevent the ruling party from going on a rampage, while the Democratic Party maintains it cannot give up the chairmanship, in order to speedily process legislation related to national tasks for the second year of the Lee Jae-myung government. On the 30th of last month, with the People Power Party absent, the Democratic Party elected chairpersons for 11 of the 18 standing committees, including the Judiciary Committee, during a plenary session. item.title: President Lee: "Strengthening Penalties for Personal Data Leaks Not a Measure Targeting Specific Companies" (李대통령 “개인정보유출 제재 강화, 특정기업 고려한 조치 아냐”)
item.description:
President Lee: "Strengthening Penalties for Personal Data Leaks Not a Measure Targeting Specific Companies" (李대통령 “개인정보유출 제재 강화, 특정기업 고려한 조치 아냐”)

President Lee Jae-myung stated on the 16th regarding personal data leaks: "The amount of fines has recently increased, and it seems some companies are claiming, 'Isn't this singling us out?'" He added, "It would be good to fully explain that this was done in accordance with laws and policies, without considering company characteristics at all." (이재명 대통령은 16일 개인정보 유출에 대해 “최근 과징금 액수가 올라갔는데, 여기에 대해 ‘나만 표적으로 하는 거 아니냐’고 주장하는 기업이 있는 것 같다”며 “기업 특성을 전혀 고려하지 않고 법과 방침에 따라 한 것이라는 점을 충분히 설명하면 좋겠다”고 했다.)

The President made these remarks while presiding over a briefing from the Personal Information Protection Commission at the Cheongwadae State Guest House, saying, "It is clear that the South Korean government's policy is to strengthen sanctions (for personal data leaks)." This appears to be aimed at Coupang, which received the largest-ever fine for a personal data leak incident. (이 대통령은 이날 청와대 영빈관에서 개인정보보호위원회 업무보고를 주재해 “명확하게 대한민국 정부의 방침이 (개인정보 유출에 대한) 제재를 강화하는 것”이라며 이같이 밝혔다. 개인정보 유출 사태로 역대 최대 규모 과징금을 받은 쿠팡을 겨냥한 것으로 보인다.)

Previously, the Personal Information Protection Commission imposed a fine of 624.6 billion won on Coupang last month for its personal data leak incident. The U.S. Congress and administration have claimed this constitutes "discrimination against an American company," escalating the Coupang case into a diplomatic issue. (앞서 개인정보보호위원회는 지난달 쿠팡의 개인정보 유출 사고에 대해 6246억원의 과징금을 부과했다. 이를 두고 미국 의회와 행정부가 “미국 기업에 대한 차별”이라고 주장하면서 쿠팡 사태가 외교 문제로 비화한 상태다.)

President Lee said, "In terms of personal data protection, relevant companies have been somewhat indifferent. Even if leaks occur, patching things up modestly costs less than security expenses, so they have practically neglected it until a large-scale leak happens." He continued, "There could also be many (data leaks) we don't know about." He added, "As we've set the policy, we need to drastically increase the scale of fines for personal data leaks or misuse so that they far exceed the cost of data protection—that's what will actually drive efforts to protect personal data." (이 대통령은 “개인정보보호 부분은 관련 기업들이 관심이 좀 떨어지고 유출되더라도 적당하게 때우는 게 보안 비용보다 적게 드니까 사실상 방치하다 대규모로 유출 사고가 발생한다”며 “우리가 모르는 (정보유출도) 많을 가능성이 있다”고 했다. 그러면서 “저희가 방침을 정한대로 개인정보 유출이나 악용에 대해 제재금을 대규모로 대폭 올려 개인정보 보호 비용을 훨씬 초과하게 만들어야 실제로는 개인정보 보호 활동을 할 거 아니냐”고 했다.)
